verses.text: There was a man named Elkanah from the Zuph family who lived in Ramathaimzophim, in the hill country of Ephraim. Elkanah was the son of Jeroham, the son of Elihu, the son of Tohu, the son of Zuph from the tribe of Ephraim.
Elkanah had 2 wives. The name of one wife was Hannah and the other wife was Peninnah. Peninnah had children but Hannah did not have any children.

Every year Elkanah left his town of Ramathaimzophim and went to Shiloh. Elkanah worshiped the Lord the All-Powerful. There in Shiloh Elkanah offered sacrifices to the Lord. The 2 sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, were the priests of the Lord in the town of Shiloh.
When Elkanah gave an offering to the Lord, he gave pieces of the meat offering to his wife Peninnah and to each of her sons and daughters.
But to Hannah, Elkanah gave a double portion because he loved her, and the LORD had closed her womb.
Peninnah would always make Hannah angry and humiliate her because the Lord did not give Hannah any children.
This happened every year when their family went to the Lord’s house at Shiloh. So, every year Peninnah would upset Hannah so much that she would begin to cry and would not eat anything.
Then Hannah’s husband, Elkanah, said to her: Hannah, why are you crying? Why don’t you eat? Why are you sad? You know you have me and that is better than having 10 sons.
After eating and drinking in Shiloh, Hannah went to the temple of the Lord. The priest Eli was sitting on a chair at the door of the tent.
Hannah was very sad. She prayed to the Lord and cried for a long time.

Hannah made a special promise to God and said, Lord, you are the one who rule everything, I am your servant, please look at me and see how sad I am. Remember me. Don't forget me. If you will give me a son, I will bring him here to belong to You for as long as he shall live and no one will shave off the hair on his head.
Hannah kept on praying to God for a long time and Eli saw her talking.
But Hannah did not speak loudly, Hannah was praying in her heart. Her lips were moving, but since she did not say the words out loud, Eli thought she was drunk.
Then Eli said to Hannah: You have had too much to drink. It is time to put away the wine.
But Hannah said to Eli: No, sir, I have not drunk wine or strong alcohol. I am very sad and I told the Lord how I feel.
Hannah said to Eli, Do not think I am a bad woman. I have talked to the Lord about all my problems and my pain.
Eli said to Hannah: Go in peace. The God of Israel will give to you what you have asked Him for.
Hannah answered: I hope that you will think well of me. Hannah went away and ate something, and she was not sad anymore.
The next morning Elkanah and his family got up, prayed to the Lord and then went back to their home in the town of Ramah. Elkanah had sex with Hannah and the Lord remembered what Hannah had asked.
It happened that Hannah became with child and gave birth to a son. Hannah named him Samuel. She said: His name is Samuel because I asked the Lord to give him to me.
Elkanah went to Shiloh to offer the sacrifice for that year and the gift he had promised to the Lord. He took his family with him.

Hannah did not go with them. She said to her husband, Elkanah: When the boy is old enough to eat solid food, I will take him to Shiloh. I will take Samuel and I will give him to the Lord to work for Him. Then Samuel can always stay there.

Her husband Elkanah said to Hannah: You must do what you think is good. You may stay home until the Samuel is old enough to eat solid food. I pray that God will do everything that He has promised you. Hannah stayed at home until her son, Samuel, stopped drinking milk from her.
When the boy ,Samuel, was old enough to eat solid food, Hannah took Samuel to the Lord’s house at Shiloh. She also took 3 bull, 10 pounds of flour, and a bottle of wine.
They sacrificed a bull and then they took the Samuel to Eli the priest.
Hannah said to Eli: Sir, do you remember me? I am the woman who was here with you and prayed to the Lord.
I prayed to have this child and the Lord has given me what I asked Him for.
And now I give this child to the Lord. He will serve the Lord all his life. Samuel worship the Lord there.

verses.text: The Philistines took The Holy Box of God, from Ebenezer to Ashdod.
The Philistines took The Holy Box of God to the temple of Dagon and they put it down next to the idol of Dagon.
When the people of Ashdod got up the next morning, they saw Dagon lying there on his face to the ground before the Holy Box of the Lord. They took Dagon and they put him back where he had been.

But when they got up the next morning, they saw that Dagon was lying down on the ground again before the Holy Box of the Lord. Dagon’s head and his hands were broken and they were lying on the doorstep. Only Dagon’s body was not broken.
This is why the priests of Dagon, and everyone else who comes into the temple of Dagon, never step on the doorstep of the temple, even until today.

The Lord punished the people of Ashdod. The Lord made them afraid by destroying their lands, and the Lord made sores come out on their bodies. The sores were on all the people of Ashdod and also on all the other people in their land.
When the people of Ashdod saw what was happening, they said: The Holy Box of the God of Israel must not stay with us, because He is the One who punishes us and our god Dagon.

They called all the leaders of the Philistines together and they asked them: What must we do with the Holy Box of the God of Israel? The leaders answered: You must take the Holy Box of the God of Israel to the town Gath. So, they took the Holy Box of the God of Israel to Gath.

But after they had taken it there, the Lord made all the people of Gath very afraid. The Lord destroyed the town and made all the people, the children and the old, very sick. They had sores in their bottom parts.
They then sent the Holy Box of God to the town of Ekron. When it came into the town, the people of Ekron shouted and said: They have sent the Holy Box of the God of Israel here to kill our people.

Then they called all the leaders of the Philistines together and said to them: You must send the Holy Box of the God of Israel back to its own place. If it stays here, it will kill all of us. The people of Ekron said this because everyone in the town was afraid of the destruction and sickness. They thought they would die. God made them suffer a lot.
Those who didn’t die were punished with sores all over their bodies. The people of Ekron cried loudly to heaven.

verses.text: The LORD said to Samuel: How long will you grieve for Saul? I have rejected Saul as king over Israel. Fill your horn with oil and go. I am sending you to Jesse in Bethlehem. I have chosen one of his sons to be king.
Samuel said: How can I go? Saul will hear about it and kill me. The LORD said: Take a young cow with you. Say: I have come to offer a sacrifice to the LORD.
Invite Jesse to the sacrifice. I will show you what to do. You will anoint the one I name to you.
Samuel did what the LORD said and went to Bethlehem. The leaders of the town came to meet Samuel. They were shaking with fear. They asked: Do you come in peace?

Samuel said: Yes, in peace. I have come to offer a sacrifice to the LORD. Make yourselves clean and come with me to the sacrifice. Samuel also made Jesse and his sons clean and invited them to the sacrifice.
When they came, Samuel saw Eliab. Samuel thought: The one the LORD has chosen must be standing here.
But the LORD said to Samuel: Do not look at Eliab's face or how tall Eliab is. I have rejected him. The LORD does not see the way people see. People look at the outside. The LORD looks at the heart.
Jesse called Abinadab and had him walk past Samuel. Samuel said: The LORD has not chosen this one either.
Jesse had Shammah walk past Samuel. Samuel said: The LORD has not chosen this one either.
Jesse had 7 of his sons walk past Samuel. Samuel said to Jesse: The LORD has not chosen any of these.
Samuel asked Jesse: Are these all your sons? Jesse said: The youngest is still out with the sheep. Samuel said to Jesse: Send for him. We will not sit down to eat until he comes here.
Jesse sent for his youngest son and brought him in. David was healthy and handsome. He had bright eyes. The LORD said to Samuel: Get up and anoint him. David is the one.
Samuel took the horn of oil and anointed David in front of his brothers. From that day on, the Spirit of the LORD came on David with power. Then Samuel went back to Ramah.
The Spirit of the LORD left Saul. The LORD sent an evil spirit that frightened and upset Saul.
Saul's servants said to him: An evil spirit from God is upsetting you.
Our king, tell us to find a man who plays the harp well. When the evil spirit from God comes on you, that man will play. Then you will feel better.
Saul said to his servants: Find me a man who plays well and bring him to me.
One servant said: I have seen a son of Jesse in Bethlehem who plays well. This young man is a brave fighter. He speaks wisely, and he is handsome. The LORD is with him.
Saul sent messengers to Jesse with this message: Send me your son David, who is with the sheep.
Jesse took a donkey loaded with bread, a bottle of wine and a young goat. Jesse sent them to Saul with his son David.
David came to Saul and stood before him. Saul loved David very much. David became the man who carried Saul's armor.
Saul sent word to Jesse: Let David stay and serve me. I am pleased with him.
Whenever the evil spirit from God came on Saul, David took his harp and played. Then Saul felt better and was well again. The evil spirit left Saul.

16.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version in the simple-English style of this Bible. Check: 'anoint' (verses 3, 12, 13) is kept as a Bible word; 'evil spirit from the LORD/God' (verses 14-16, 23) follows the Hebrew; 'ruddy' in verse 12 is rendered 'healthy, with bright eyes'; 'armourbearer' in verse 21 is rendered 'the man who carried Saul's armor'.
